court: Supreme Court, General Term, First Department
holding_summary: Defendant, having represented to plaintiff during purchase negotiations that his remaining Fifth Avenue houses were restricted to and would always be first-class private residences, was equitably estopped from enlarging the adjoining house (over the shared party-wall) not as a private residence but for business purposes as part of a family hotel; the court restrained that use as an unauthorized encroachment on plaintiff's easement rights, though it noted defendant could still build on the party-wall to enlarge a private residence.

quotes.text: it is the use of the existing easement for purposes antagonistical to the expressed design of the defendant in building the houses, made patent by his statements and representations, which is complained of, and by which the house adjoining the plaintiff’s, to the prejudice of her property, as shown by the evidence, was enlarged, not as a private residence, but for business purposes, namely, as part of a family hotel.

Our judgment is, therefore, it appearing that plaintiff did not assent to the use of the party-wall between her and the adjoining premises for the erection of the additional stories which were made for business purposes, her right to protection from such a use by the defendant exists, and in equity and good conscience should be enforced

We do not wish to be understood, however, as declaring it to be our judgment that the defendant would have no right to build upon the party-wall," if the object were to enlarge his house as a private residence.
